tco-build-tco.d: Total Cost of Ownership for building your own data center over the analysis period. Includes CAPEX (land, construction, M&E) plus all annual OPEX (energy, staff, maintenance). Higher upfront but lower per-kW cost at scale.

tco-colo-tco.d: Total cost of colocating in a third-party facility over the period. Includes monthly rack/cage fees, cross-connect charges, remote hands, and power charges. No CAPEX — cost scales with committed power draw in kW.

tco-cloud-tco.d: Total cloud infrastructure cost over the period. Based on on-demand or reserved instance pricing per kW of compute equivalent. Typically highest at scale but offers maximum flexibility and no CAPEX commitment.

tco-best-option.d: The deployment model with the lowest total cost of ownership over the selected analysis period. Winner is highlighted in green. Compare all three options to understand where crossover points occur at different scales and time horizons.

tco-build-capex.d: One-time capital expenditure to construct and commission the owned facility. Includes site acquisition, civil works, M&E systems, IT infrastructure, and project management. Amortized over the asset useful life in financial models.

tco-yr-1-opex-build.d: First-year annual operating expenditure for the owned facility. Includes energy costs (IT + overhead), staffing, preventive maintenance contracts, insurance, and property tax. Grows each year with the escalation rate.

tco-cost-per-kw.d: Effective all-in cost per kW of IT capacity for the best-option deployment model. Calculated as total TCO divided by IT load (kW) divided by years. Industry benchmark: $150-500/kW/yr for owned; $300-600 for colo; $500-1200+ for cloud.

tco-breakeven-year.d: The year at which cumulative Build TCO equals cumulative Colo TCO. Before this year, colo is cheaper (no CAPEX). After this year, owning becomes cheaper due to lower per-kW OPEX at scale. Typical DC breakeven is years 4-8.

cx-total-cx-cost.d: Total commissioning and testing cost across all disciplines (electrical, mechanical, controls, safety, integration). Includes CxA fees, OEM startup costs, testing labor, instrumentation, and 15% contingency. Based on ASHRAE Guideline 0 scope.

cx-duration-weeks.d: Total commissioning schedule from system installation through Level 4 or 5 integrated systems testing. Duration scales with facility size, tier level, and redundancy. Tier IV and 2N facilities require significantly more IST scenarios and verification cycles.

cx-cost-per-kw.d: Total commissioning cost normalized to IT load capacity. Industry benchmark: $30-80/kW for Tier II, $80-150/kW for Tier III, $150-250/kW for Tier IV. Higher density and higher tier drive up cost per kW due to more complex IST scenario coverage.

cx-of-capex.d: Commissioning cost as a percentage of total facility CAPEX. Industry standard is 1-3% for Tier II-III and 3-5% for Tier IV. A ratio below 1% typically indicates under-scoped commissioning, increasing operational risk and warranty claim complexity.
